read.sections.0.text.back: Most cities started as small places. A town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a port, a railway line or a factory. Better transport also helps, because people and goods can move in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the national capital. This created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do them. A change like this is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.text.source: Most cities start small. A town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a harbour, a railway or factories. Better transport also helps, because it lets people and goods move in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital city. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do them. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.

read.sections.1.heading.back: Real cities grow in the same way
read.sections.1.heading.source: Real cities grew in similar ways

read.sections.1.text.back: Many real cities grew in the same way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway line. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. In 1980, only about 30,000 people lived in Shenzhen, in southern China. Then the government made it a special area for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there to work. Today, it is among the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport caused the population to increase.
read.sections.1.text.source: Many real cities grew in a similar way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. Today it is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.

In both places, jobs and transport made the population increase.

read.sections.2.text.back: Growth can bring benefits to a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more houses, clean water and health care. Services are help that people need, such as a clinic or a school. Infrastructure is the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and electricity lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview had new houses, a school and bus routes. But people waited a long time at the only clinic, because the clinic did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan early.
read.sections.2.text.source: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more homes, clean water and health care. A service is help that people need, like a clinic or a school. Infrastructure means the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview has new houses, a school and bus routes. But people wait a long time at the only clinic, because it did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan ahead.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Growth can bring benefits. Big cities have more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need houses and clean water. They need services such as clinics. They need infrastructure, such as roads and pipes. All of this takes time to build. In Year 15, people waited a long time at Bayview's clinic. The clinic did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.

'Carts' is translated as 'kereta kuda' (horse carts). Check both against the video. Back-translation check: Translator flag stands: 'kereta kuda' (horse carts) adds 'horse' to 'carts', and 'alam semula jadi' (nature) stands in for 'the land'. Check both against the video.
watch.summary.back: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of humans live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, humans began farming. They could grow food, so they settled in villages. Later, better ways of farming produced surplus food. Not everyone needed to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade also grew, with horse carts, ships, roads and ports. Long after that, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to get rid of rubbish. In the future, more people will live in cities. The video says that cities must provide enough food, toilets and schools for everyone. Cities must also protect nature. Some of the ideas are gardens on roofs, tall buildings, and energy from the sun and wind.
watch.summary.source: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of all people live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, people began to farm. They could grow food, so they stayed in villages. Later, better farming made extra food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade grew too, with carts, ships, roads and ports. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to take away waste. In the future, even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must give everyone enough food, toilets and schools. They must also protect the land. Ideas include rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and power from the sun and wind.
